1.explanation: We create a minimal artifact set with a fake main document and two network requests (one to google-analytics.com and one to fonts.gstatic.com) that have non-zero DNS+TCP times. We then invoke the uses-rel-preconnect audit directly. Even if your real page HTML includes `<link rel=preconnect>` tags, the audit logic (in Lighthouse 3.0.3) doesn’t read the DOM to detect them, so it still returns those origins with positive savings. Running this script reproduces the false positive.
1.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse’s "Avoid multiple, costly round trips to any origin" opportunity audit (`uses-rel-preconnect`) runs against a page that already includes `<link rel="preconnect">` tags for those origins, it still flags them as missing. In other words, even though the page’s HTML has preconnect hints for “https://www.google-analytics.com” and “https://fonts.gstatic.com”, Lighthouse reports them under the opportunity with non-zero potential savings.
